tagline: Sync product management in Asana with engineering execution in Linear
metaTitle: Asana + Linear Integration: Asana Tasks to Linear Issues
metaDescription: See engineering progress on Asana timelines. GAIA creates Linear issues from Asana tasks and syncs cycles to milestones. See the setup steps.
intro:
Product teams often live in Asana for its project planning capabilities while engineering teams prefer Linear for its speed and developer-centric workflow. The gap between the two creates a constant synchronization problem — product managers manually copy specs into engineering issues, engineers close those issues but the project plan still shows tasks as open, and leadership lacks a unified view of what is shipped versus what is planned.

GAIA bridges the two so product decisions automatically flow into engineering backlogs and engineering progress automatically surfaces in product timelines. When a product manager marks a task as ready for engineering, GAIA creates the corresponding issue with full context. When engineers close an issue, GAIA updates the task status so the product roadmap stays accurate.

This integration is built for product-engineering teams who want to keep their preferred tools while eliminating the coordination overhead that comes from running two disconnected systems.

useCases.title: Create Linear issues from Asana tasks
useCases.description: When a product manager marks a task as Ready for Engineering, GAIA automatically creates an issue in the appropriate team's backlog with the task title, description, and any attached specs.

useCases.title: Reflect engineering progress in product timelines
useCases.description: When an issue moves to In Progress or Done, GAIA updates the corresponding task status so product managers see accurate engineering progress without needing to check the engineering backlog directly.

useCases.title: Sync sprint cycles to milestones
useCases.description: GAIA maps sprint timelines to milestone dates, giving the product team visibility into engineering cadences and ensuring release planning reflects what engineering can realistically deliver.

useCases.title: Bug escalation from Linear to Asana
useCases.description: When a high-priority bug is filed, GAIA creates a corresponding task for the product team, prompting them to assess customer impact and reprioritize the roadmap if necessary.

useCases.title: Blocked issue alerts across teams
useCases.description: When an issue is blocked waiting on product decisions, GAIA creates a task for the responsible product manager with context and a deadline, preventing engineering from stalling silently.

howItWorks.step: Connect Asana and Linear to GAIA
howItWorks.description: Authorize GAIA to access your workspace and organization. Configure which projects map to which teams and how statuses correspond between the two tools.

howItWorks.step: Define trigger conditions and field mappings
howItWorks.description: Set the conditions that trigger syncs, such as a task reaching a specific section or an issue changing state, and map fields like priority, assignee, and description between the two tools.

howItWorks.step: GAIA keeps product and engineering aligned
howItWorks.description: GAIA monitors both tools continuously and propagates changes in real time, so product managers and engineers always work from a shared, accurate understanding of project status.

faqs.question: Can GAIA sync Asana project sections to Linear cycles?
faqs.answer: Yes. GAIA can map project sections to cycles or projects on the engineering side, and update issue assignments as tasks move through your workflow stages.

faqs.question: What if the same feature is tracked differently in each tool?
faqs.answer: You can define explicit mappings between tasks and issues by linking them manually the first time. After that, GAIA maintains the link and syncs updates automatically.

faqs.question: Does GAIA sync issue comments back to the tasks?
faqs.answer: GAIA can append a summary of comment activity on the issue to the task description or post it as a task comment, keeping product managers informed of engineering discussions without requiring access to the issues themselves.
